title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 748-751). Grothendieck has an abstract 'structure' (32). It consists of a profinite group M acting by automorphisms of L-structures on an arithmetic-type fundamental group, with a filtration of normal subgroups Pi ⊂ G ⊂ M. On the next page the quotients are named T = G/Pi, Gamma = M/G, N = M/Pi.

The model is the fundamental group of a modular multiplicity (moduli stack of curves) over Q:
- T is its 'geometric' part (the profinite Teichmüller group).
- T_0 is its 'transcendental' part (the discrete Teichmüller / mapping class group).
- Gamma is Gal(Qbar/Q).
- A discrete 'Teichmüller discontinuity group' G_0 (written gothic G_0) sits inside M.

On p.751 he imposes a cyclotomic condition (33)-(34): the cyclotomic action factors as a character chi_Gamma : Gamma -> Zhat^*, with a struck-out clause that its image be open. He also fixes a linear algebraic group G_Q with a character chi_G : G_Q -> G_m. He then considers homomorphisms rho : M -> G(A_Q), A_Q the adeles, satisfying conditions 1°-4°. Condition 3° is strengthened to '3° forte' (compatibility with the Teichmüller discontinuity group G_0).

This page.

(i) Strong 3° says the restriction of rho to G_0 factors through the rational points: there is G_0 -> G(Q) such that the square (35) commutes:
  G_0 -> M
  G(Q) -> G(A_Q)
with vertical maps G_0 -> G(Q) and M -> G(A_Q). The discrete transcendental part therefore lands in the diagonally embedded rational points, exactly as an arithmetic group sits inside an adelic group.

(ii) He names the structures of type (32) 'structures de Galois-Teichmüller', provisionally. A margin note admits he later forgot to build the discontinuity condition (the datum G_0) into the definition of the structure itself.

(iii) For G a smooth algebraic group over Q (automatically smooth in characteristic 0), a homomorphism M -> G(A_Q) satisfying 1°, 2°, strong 3° and 4° is called a 'lien de Lie' of the Galois-Teichmüller structure. It is an adelic, algebraic-group-valued realization with a rational structure on the discrete Teichmüller part.

(iv) He begins defining algebraic envelopes. M_Q is the group scheme G_Q (better: the Zariski-closure envelope). Next he begins to define the subgroup scheme generated by the image of G_0 -> G(Q), i.e. its Zariski closure.

The next page continues:
- Pi_Q ⊂ G_Q ⊂ M_Q, normal in M_Q;
- quotients T_Q, Gamma_Q, N_Q;
- the exact sequence 1 -> T_Q -> N_Q -> Gamma_Q -> 1;
- chi_c : G_Q -> G_m is an epimorphism and factors through Gamma_Q.

Purpose. To attach to the Galois action on the Teichmüller tower a Q-algebraic 'Lie' envelope (a motivic-Galois-like algebraic group). Its rational structure comes from the discrete mapping class group and its adelic points receive the arithmetic group. This is the Lie/algebraic shadow of the Galois-Teichmüller group.
errors: The margin note acknowledges a gap: the discontinuity datum (G_0 and its compatibility) was not built into the definition of the 'structure de Galois-Teichmüller' itself, so the definition of 'lien de Lie' presupposes data not yet formally part of the structure.
'Smooth' is redundant for algebraic groups over Q (characteristic 0, Cartier).

'Subgroup scheme generated by the image' of a subgroup of G(Q) must mean Zariski closure. For the image of M, which lies in G(A_Q) and not in G(Q), 'generated' needs a precise meaning: e.g. the smallest Q-subgroup H with rho(M) ⊂ H(A_Q). This is left implicit.

The next page's claim that chi_c is an epimorphism needs the image of Gamma in Zhat^* (hence in A^*) to be infinite, so that it is not contained in some mu_n. Openness was the struck-out hypothesis on p.751, so it is used without being kept as an assumption.
Transcription: the diagram is labelled (35), not (31).

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'structure de Galois-Teichmüller': a profinite extension of Gal(Qbar/Q) by a geometric Teichmüller-type group, with a dense discrete 'transcendental' subgroup (mapping class group) and a cyclotomic character
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on profinite mapping class groups / Teichmüller tower; Galois-Teichmüller group (GT) formalism
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and Galois action; the specific axiomatic name 'structure de Galois-Teichmüller' appears unpublished

ideas.what: 'Lien de Lie': adelic representation M -> G(A_Q) whose restriction to the discrete Teichmüller group factors through G(Q) (diagonally embedded)
ideas.modern_name: Rational/adelic algebraic realization; analogous to relative completion with Q-structure from Betti side; comparison of Betti and adelic/ℓ-adic realizations of a motivic Galois group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hain (relative completion of mapping class groups, 1990s), Hain-Matsumoto (weighted completion of Galois groups, 2003), Deligne (motivic fundamental group, 1989)

ideas.what: Algebraic envelopes M_Q ⊃ G_Q ⊃ Pi_Q as Zariski closures, with quotient exact sequence 1->T_Q->N_Q->Gamma_Q->1 and cyclotomic character Gamma_Q -> G_m
ideas.modern_name: Zariski-closure (algebraic hull) of Galois image; weighted/relative completion; motivic Galois group of mixed Tate motives mapping onto G_m
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (ℓ-adic algebraic hulls), Deligne, Hain-Matsumoto, Deligne-Goncharov

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines an adelic (all primes at once) algebraic-group realization of the Galois-Teichmüller structure. The discrete mapping class group is required to land in G(Q), in the way an arithmetic group sits in an adelic group. He then forms Q-algebraic envelopes with a cyclotomic character onto G_m. This anticipates Hain-Matsumoto's weighted/relative completion programme, but in an adelic, Q-rational form rather than one ℓ at a time.
missed.quote: un lien M → G(A_Q) satisfaisant les conditions 1°) 2°) 3°)(forte) 4°) est dit un "lien de Lie" de la structure de Galois-Teichmüller
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Hain-Matsumoto and the motivic mapping-class-group literature work ℓ-adically, or via Betti-de Rham comparison. An adelic formulation with rational structure forced by the topological mapping class group is a distinct compatibility condition, a 'rationality across all ℓ'. It does not seem to be formalized as such in the literature.

missed.claim: By the margin note's own admission, the definition of Galois-Teichmüller structure omits the discontinuity (discrete Teichmüller group) data. The Lie-link theory is set up only sketchily: existence and universal links, and comparison with GT/grt, are not addressed on this page.
missed.quote: Oublié par la suite à introduire les conditions de discontinuité sur structure
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A universal 'lien de Lie' would be a candidate algebraic Galois-Teichmüller group over Q. Comparing it with Drinfeld's GT(Q) / grt and with the motivic Galois group of mixed Tate motives over Z is an open-ended thread.

deep.surprise_reason: The page introduces an unpublished, named axiomatics ('structures de Galois-Teichmüller', 'liens de Lie'): adelic algebraic-group realizations with a Q-rational discrete Teichmüller part, followed by Zariski-closure envelopes. It clearly anticipates relative/weighted completion and motivic ideas later developed by Hain-Matsumoto, Deligne and others. However, it is only a definitional sketch with an admitted gap, and closely related notions now exist.
transcription_corrections: First word likely 'lien' (as in 'un lien G_0 → G(Q)'), not 'tels'; 'rendant commutatif le diagramme' is correct.
'groupe algébrique [-...-] lisse' : reading 'groupe algébrique lisse sur Q' plausible; 'est dit un "lien de Lie"'.
Margin note reads approximately: 'Oublié par la suite à introduire des conditions de discontinuité sur structure'.
